name: Florida

benefitCategories.medical: Reasonable and necessary treatment; managed care arrangements may apply
benefitCategories.temporaryTotal: 66 2/3% of wages up to $1,197/week (2024); max 104 weeks
benefitCategories.temporaryPartial: 80% of wage loss up to max; max 104 weeks combined with TT
benefitCategories.impairmentBenefits: 75% of TTD rate × 2 weeks per % permanent impairment (Fla. Uniform Impairment Guide)
benefitCategories.permanentTotal: 66 2/3% of wages to max; lifetime if catastrophic; otherwise ends at 75 or 401 weeks
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: 50% of wages to spouse; additional for children; $7,500 burial

workersCompensation.initialClaimForm: DWC-1 (First Report of Injury) by employer; Employee Notice of Injury to employer

appealLevels.name: Judge of Compensation Claims (JCC)
appealLevels.body: Office of Judges of Compensation Claims (DOAH)
appealLevels.deadline: 2 years from injury or last payment

workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: DWC investigations; stop-work orders; carrier compliance audits
workersCompensation.penalties: Stop-work orders for uninsured ($1,000/day penalty); fraud prosecution

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Florida has no state temporary disability insurance program

programs.name: Reemployment Assistance (Unemployment)
programs.eligibility: Unemployed through no fault; able and available to work
programs.note: Not available if disabled; WC may preclude

programs.name: Florida Medicaid
programs.eligibility: Low-income; Florida did not expand Medicaid under ACA

civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Retaliation prohibited for filing complaints, testifying, or opposing unlawful practices

laborStandards.authority: Federal DOL/WHD handles FLSA; Florida has no state minimum wage enforcement agency (voter-approved minimum wage self-executing)

occupationalSafety.authority: Florida is not a state plan state; OSHA covers private sector

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 2 years from injury or last payment/treatment
filingDeadlines.lawsuit: 1 year from FCHR determination or 180 days if no determination

evidentiaryStandards.wc: Preponderance of evidence; clear and convincing for psychiatric claims

judicialReview.wc: JCC → First DCA → Florida Supreme Court (discretionary)
judicialReview.civilRights: FCHR investigation → Determination → Circuit Court (or elect DOAH)
judicialReview.eeoc: May dual-file with EEOC; federal court option

specialConsiderations.reforms2003: Significant 2003 reforms tightened benefits; eliminated permanent total for under-75 non-catastrophic; greater weight of evidence standard
specialConsiderations.medicalAccessIssues: Managed care/network restrictions may limit provider choice
specialConsiderations.constructionEmphasis: Strict construction industry requirements; all construction employers must carry coverage
